question: Why does the 2026-09-16 n=200 audit run 1.5-2.5x worse than the July 2026-07-19 n=200 figures the site publishes on the four matched axes?

verdict.persons_and_pins: CONVENTION. Under July's own rubric (addressee/place-in-author-field routed to the issue register, office-for-person and one-leaf slot drift graded PART), September's stratum-A wrongs collapse to persons 3/147 = 2.1% and pins 0/84 = 0.0%, matching the published 2.5% and 1.0%.
verdict.dates_and_substance: JULY UNDER-CALLED. Not convention: all 9 September date-wrongs and all 13 substance-wrongs on unchanged fields are ERR under July's own rubric (wrong day/month/year; misread figures, names, quotes). A seeded 30-record slice of July's own sample regraded at the leaf at September depth yields dates 4/30 = 13.3% and substance 5/30 = 16.7% against July's published 6.5% and 5.5%, reproducing September's stratum-A rates (13.6% / 17.3%). Three of the four new errors are crop- or arithmetic-proven.
verdict.population: REAL BUT CUSHIONING. The DB grew ~19.8k -> 34,895 between audits. The 89 sampled records added after July grade at July-like rates (dates 5.6%, persons 3.0%, substance 6.7%, pins 0.0%). The newer half of the catalog is measurably cleaner; restricting September to July's population makes the discrepancy wider, not narrower.
verdict.real_change: MINOR AND FAVORABLE. 27 of 76 old-stratum wrong judgements sit on fields edited since July; every case examined (ca11-d233/d277/d327, ca12-d327/d409, ca14-d48, ca55-d224, ca63-d419/d502) is a partial repair of a row that was more wrong in July, not a regression.

bottom_line: The published July figures were too generous on dates and substance, by roughly a factor of two on the population they measured, because the July grader verified at reading resolution and echoed record values where September re-derives digits at magnification. September's numbers survive regrading; publish those (both conventions, with the population note) and retire the July figures.

september_strata.definition: July population = union of ca-catalog-export.json and catalog/*.md at commit b8512b49e (2026-07-17); eligibility = item grain, no verified stamp, rating <= 2, scan link (the July README criteria).

desk_regrade_of_september_wrongs_under_j.date: 9 of 9 stay ERR (wrong day/month/year: e.g. ca21-d301 1820 not 1830, ca56-d355 Febrero not September, ca34-d543 En.o 28 not 24)
desk_regrade_of_september_wrongs_under_j.persons: 3 of 7 stay ERR (ca15-d491 Arvide not Avila, ca20-d51 Fr. Antonio Anzar not 'San Luis Rey alcaldes', ca22-d2036 Pedro Garrido not 'Pedro Parrilla'); 4 drop to the July issue-register/PART classes (ca13-d214, ca13-d272, ca34-d52 place-or-addressee-in-author; ca14-d131 blank recipient)
desk_regrade_of_september_wrongs_under_j.substance: 13 of 13 stay ERR (figures, names, quotes: $83,741 not $82,741; 267 not 257 pelts; $8,427 not $1,427; Osuna not Avila; Anza not Ayala)
desk_regrade_of_september_wrongs_under_j.pins: 0 of 4 stay ERR (ca8-d257, ca63-d127, ca63-d129 are one-leaf slot drift, which July's final tranche graded PART on C-A 63 itself; ca8-d288's document is on the cited leaf)

july_slice_regrade.method: random.Random(20260920).sample(range(1,201),30) over July's committed n=200; 5 known July ERRs reused; 25 records regraded against the leaf at September depth using the JULY-17 field values

new_errors_found.proof: scale-1 crop; the day's first digit is a 2 unlike the 3s of '1833' on the same line; July's note itself echoed 'May 30'
scale-1 crop; final year digit is a 9 with descender; next entry on the leaf is 1820; the Reyna de los Angeles war-supplies charter fits 1819
arithmetic closes only as 2640 - 69 = 2571; scale-1 crop shows a closed 0, and the commission glyph reads 3
marginal/convention case: July saw the discrepancy and logged it as a note without grading; September counts a leaf-contradicted count as WRONG

additional_finding_orig_page: The September orig_page dimension (9.3% wrong) measures citation correctness July's PIN axis never measured. In C-A 11 and C-A 52 the orig_page field systematically holds the copybook folio, not the tomo page Bancroft cites (ca11-d105 field 162 vs leaf foot pp.387-8; ca11-d273 field 248 vs p.628; ca52-d16 field 56 vs pp.373-4). July's notes accepted the folio as 'matching'.
caveats: The 30-record slice also returned zero UNVERIFIABLE judgements; all 25 leaf targets were readable.
The ca42-d44 flip is convention-flavored, not blindness: July recorded the discrepancy in its note.

July population reconstruction is approximate: the July-17 export (19,755) and catalog tree (18,674) disagree with the July README's stated 19,910; the union was used. Stratum results were stable across all three definitions tried.
No live-site change was made. Nothing here is published.
